gaps.note: The supplier FEOC packet should include all manufactured-product certifications and a material assistance cost ratio. The PV module (Sunvale) certification has not been received, and no MACR calculation has been prepared.

The PWA report covers only January 12, 2026 through September 15, 2026. It does not address any pre-2026 construction work or the period through placed-in-service, now forecast for February 2027. It also gives no evidence that the $370,800 cure payment has been made.

The PWA report refers to wage determinations 'for the county' but does not name the county or state used. That is needed to confirm the correct Montgomery County, Illinois determinations were applied.
The cost segregation report does not state the project site location, which would be expected for a basis study tied to the project.
The site memo gives '100%' as the share of nameplate capacity in the tract but does not state the AC or DC nameplate capacity.
The construction monitoring report does not restate the project's AC or DC capacity.

The manufacturer letter gives no evidence of the significance of the off-site work, its cost, or its continuity, given the later rewind after the factory acceptance test failure. Counsel's promised beginning-of-construction memo is not in the data room.

questions.prompt: Which beginning-of-construction date should Buyer rely on for pricing and diligence: off-site transformer manufacture (December 22, 2025) or on-site pile installation (January 12, 2026)?
questions.context: The 2025 date rests on off-site work on a custom transformer under a binding written contract dated December 10, 2025. The IE has not reviewed these records, and the transformer failed factory acceptance testing and is being rewound, which bears on continuity. On-site physical work began January 12, 2026. A 2026 start pushes the domestic content threshold to 50%, so 47.8% fails and the credit rate drops from 50% to 40%. A 2026 start also makes the FEOC material assistance rules apply, while the module certification and MACR are missing.

evidence.text: Physical manufacture of the transformer, beginning with cutting and stacking of the custom core, commenced at our facility on December 22, 2025
On-site physical work of a significant nature, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
We have not reviewed the manufacturer's records and express no opinion on the tax treatment of off-site work.
If construction is determined to have begun in 2026, the applicable threshold would be 50% and the Project would not qualify at the computed adjusted percentage.

options.label: Accept off-site transformer work: construction began December 22, 2025
options.consequence: The domestic content bonus qualifies at 47.8% against 45%, and FEOC material assistance rules do not apply. The credit stays at 50%, or $68,200,000 on $136,400,000. Buyer relies on unreviewed off-site records and should condition closing on the counsel memo and manufacturer continuity evidence.

options.label: Rely on on-site physical work: construction began January 12, 2026
options.consequence: The domestic content bonus fails (47.8% against 50%), reducing the rate to 40%, or $54,560,000 of credit and a $51,013,600 purchase price at $0.935. FEOC rules apply, and the module certification and MACR become closing requirements.

options.label: Defer: require the beginning-of-construction memo and IE review before deciding
options.consequence: No value is resolved yet. The credit amount stays uncertain between $54,560,000 and $68,200,000 until the evidence is delivered.

questions.prompt: How should Buyer treat the unmet apprenticeship labor-hour requirement and the proposed $370,800 cure payment?
questions.context: Apprentice hours are 13.2% against the required 15.0%, a 7,416-hour shortfall, with no Good Faith Effort exception documented. The Seller intends, but has not yet made, a $370,800 cure payment. Without PWA, the §48E rate falls to 6% base plus 2% for each bonus. The binder excludes known PWA deficiencies.

evidence.text: The labor hour requirement is not satisfied for the period reviewed. The Seller has not documented a Good Faith Effort exception for the shortfall.
As of the report date, the payment has not been made; Seller has indicated it intends to make the payment before the placed-in-service date.

options.label: Treat as curable: make proof of cure payment and an updated full-period PWA report a condition precedent
options.consequence: The 5x multiplier is preserved once the cure is paid and documented. Buyer remains exposed if the cure is not paid or later shortfalls arise, and the insurance exclusion may leave this uninsured.

options.label: Treat PWA as not met unless and until cured before closing
options.consequence: The credit rate falls to 10% (6% base plus 2% plus 2%), or $13,640,000 on $136,400,000. In practice this means not closing until the cure is evidenced, or repricing.
